question.problem:
Find the equation of the tangent line to the polar curve $r=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\theta )$ at $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6},$ given that 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta )+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\theta )}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\theta )}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
To find the equation of the tangent line to a polar curve at a point $P,$ we follow four steps:

**Step 1**: Calculate the derivative $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}:$

In this case, we're given that

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta )+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\theta )}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\theta )}.
$$

**Step 2**: Find the slope of the tangent at $P:$

The slope of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =\pi /6} \\  & =\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta )+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\theta )}{3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\theta )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\theta )} \\  & =\frac{[3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})]}{[3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})]} \\  & =\frac{[3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})]}{[3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})]} \\  & =\frac{(3\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot 0+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot 1)}{(3\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot 0-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})}{(-\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =-\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P:$

We compute the $xy$-coordinates of $P$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\theta )\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ {y}_{1} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\theta )\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of $P$ are $(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\frac{1}{2}).$ 

**Step 4**: Using point-slope form, find the equation of the tangent:

We find the equation of the tangent as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-\frac{1}{2} & =-\sqrt{3}\cdot (x-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\ y-\frac{1}{2} & =-\sqrt{3}\,x+\frac{3}{2} \\ y & =-\sqrt{3}x+2\end{aligned}
$$
